what: Pennsylvania's selection criteria for Low Income Housing Tax Credits, transcribed from the Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency's own documents. The points, tiers and caps are PHFA's. The `basis` of each line (who or what decides it) and the short wording of each rule are this project's reading, written so the sheet can be filled in for a place. PHFA scores every application itself; nothing here is an award or a prediction of one.

pool.label: Urban pool
pool.why: PHFA lists the City of Pittsburgh among the urban areas with more than 25,000 people, so a Pittsburgh application competes in the urban pool and the urban tiers below apply. At least 25% of the urban pool is first set aside for municipalities other than Philadelphia.

bases.place: Measured here from where the place is
bases.lookup: Depends on the address; a score to look up
bases.site: Depends on the parcel that is chosen
bases.design: Decided in the design and the unit mix
bases.partners: Needs a letter, a commitment or an approval from others
bases.team: Who is on the development team
bases.finance: How the development is paid for

sources.title: Tab 3, Selection Criteria Self-Scoring (PHFA, PDF dated 2024-12-04)

remarks: PHFA states the 9% minimum two ways: 125 points in the scoring table and on the self-scoring sheet, 120 points in sections 4.3 and 4.5 of the plan. This sheet uses 125.
Development Cost Savings (section E, 10 points) is suspended for 2025/2026 and is not part of the 232.
The items for new construction in section A add up to 36; PHFA states the section as 37 because preservation can reach 17 in A.2.
The self-scoring sheet totals section D as 91 in one place and 93 in another; its items add up to 93.

Passing the minimum does not win an award. Credits go to the highest scores within each pool and preference, and a tie goes to the application with the larger share of units at or below 50% of area median income.

items.label: Area of opportunity
items.rule: Up to 13 points where the market study shows low poverty, few affordable homes (subsidized or not), little affordable housing built in the past 20 years, jobs close by, a strong housing market and a high share of owners.

items.label: School performance
items.rule: The public senior high school serving the site: combined average proficiency in English, mathematics and science of 70% to 80% earns 1 point, over 80% earns 2.

items.label: Underserved area for seniors
items.rule: Up to 15 points where many seniors qualify for affordable housing, affordable homes are few, little has been built in 20 years, and health care, shops, home health agencies and hospitals are close.

items.label: Community revitalization plan
items.rule: A letter from a local government official saying how the development contributes to a named, adopted revitalization plan. A zoning or land use plan does not count.

items.label: Funding commitments in the area
items.rule: Evidence of significant funding commitments from other housing, community or economic development programs as part of a major investment in the area. Requests made in this application do not count.

items.label: Mixed-income housing
items.rule: At least 15% and no more than 50% of the units are market rate, with a shown financial benefit. Not available with income averaging.

items.label: Transit-oriented design
items.rule: The site is within one-half mile of a completed or planned fixed-route public transit stop, or in an area with a no-cost accessible alternative.

items.label: Walkability
items.rule: Walk Score of 70 to 79 earns 1 point, 80 or more earns 2 (urban tiers). Scattered sites use an average weighted by units.

items.label: Funding commitments in the area
items.rule: Evidence of significant funding commitments from other housing, community or economic development programs as part of a major investment in the area.

items.label: Risk of loss to the market
items.rule: Section 8 project-based or similar restrictions expire within 12 months of the application, with occupancy above 90% over the last five years.

items.label: Risk of loss to physical needs
items.rule: More than 15 years past loan closing and placed-in-service, with a major building component to replace or an immediate health or safety need.

items.label: Mixed-income housing
items.rule: At least 15% and no more than 50% of the units are market rate, with a shown financial benefit. Not available with income averaging.

items.label: Transit-oriented design
items.rule: The site is within one-half mile of a completed or planned fixed-route public transit stop, or in an area with a no-cost accessible alternative.

items.label: Walkability
items.rule: Walk Score of 70 to 79 earns 1 point, 80 or more earns 2 (urban tiers).

items.label: Addresses social inequities
items.rule: The Social Inequities and Local Disparities Certification plus a narrative of initiatives and outreach beyond a normal rent-up.

items.label: Homes at or below 50% of area median income
items.rule: Share of all units, market-rate units included, that are affordable to and occupied by households at or below 50% of area median income: over 10% earns 4 points, then 4 more for each further 10 points of share, to 20 points above 50%.

items.label: Supportive services

options.label: Services plan meeting the four minimum factors
The same, funded for 15 years and with the minimum on-site staffing

items.rule: A services plan for the whole resident population for the compliance period. The four minimum factors earn 7 points; a 15-year funding commitment and one hour of on-site staff a week for every five units can add 5.

items.label: Accessible units

options.label: Twice the required number (preservation: 5% more of all units)
Three times the required number (preservation: 10% more of all units)

items.rule: New construction or substantial rehabilitation: two times the fully accessible units otherwise required earns 5 points, three times earns 10 (always rounded up). Preservation: raising them by 5% of all units earns 5, by 10% earns 10.

items.label: Homes for large families
items.rule: Affordable units with three or more bedrooms as a share of all rental units: over 15% earns 6 points, over 20% earns 8, over 25% earns 10 (urban tiers). Not available to buildings of seven or more stories or to senior housing.

items.label: Broadband and internet access
items.rule: A device sharing program, free WiFi in public areas, and either free internet in every unit or an internet utility allowance.

items.label: Section 811 units
items.rule: At least 10% of the units, or five units in an urban area if that is more, set aside as Section 811 one-bedroom units for people with disabilities aged 18 to 61, two of them accessible at the 50% rent. Must be named in the Intent to Submit and accepted by PHFA.

items.label: Brownfield site
items.rule: A former industrial or commercial property where reuse is complicated by a hazardous substance, with the cleanup inside the project. Lead paint, asbestos or a storage tank alone does not count.

items.label: Blight remediation or residential infill
items.rule: A vacant, previously developed site (or one with a dilapidated structure to be demolished) in an existing residential or mixed-use neighborhood with infrastructure in place, built at the type and scale of its neighbors. It must be at least 51% of the project's floor area.

items.label: Adaptive reuse of an existing building
items.rule: A vacant non-residential building turned into housing, making up at least 51% of the residential floor area.

items.label: Green building certification
items.rule: Certification under Enterprise Green Communities 2020, LEED v4 Silver, or ICC 700-2020 National Green Building Standard Silver (preservation has its own list).

items.label: Energy efficiency goal

options.label: Zero Energy Ready Home, self-certified
HERS index lower than Energy Star requires
Zero Energy Ready Home, certified by the U.S. Department of Energy program
Passive House, certified

items.rule: One only: a reduced HERS index earns 5 points, Zero Energy Ready Home 8 when certified or 3 when self-certified, certified Passive House 10.

items.label: Build America, Buy America
items.rule: Only when applying for PHFA loan resources (PennHOMES, Housing Trust Fund or PHARE): agree to follow the federal Build America, Buy America requirements.

items.label: Experience of the applicant

options.label: Experienced housing consultant instead
1 to 4 tax credit developments placed in service
5 to 10
11 or more

items.rule: Tax credit developments with a placed-in-service package submitted, averaged by ownership share when there are co-applicants: 1 to 4 earns 3 points, 5 to 10 earns 6, 11 or more earns 9. An experienced housing consultant earns 3 instead.

items.label: Experience of the management agent

options.label: Experienced management consultant instead
25 to 150 tax credit units managed
301 or more

items.rule: Tax credit units managed: 25 to 150 earns 3 points, 151 to 300 earns 6, 301 or more earns 9. An experienced housing management consultant earns 3 instead.

items.label: Attorney with tax credit experience
items.rule: 2 points.

items.label: Experienced general contractor
items.rule: 2 points.

items.label: Experienced architect

options.label: Design architect or contract administration architect
Both

items.rule: 1 point for the design architect and 1 for the construction contract administration architect.

items.label: Small diverse, veteran or small business on the team

options.label: Management agent, self-certified small business
Joint venture at 30% or more, self-certified
Management agent, certified with the state
Joint venture at 51% or more, self-certified
Joint venture at 30% or more, certified with the state
Owner or developer, self-certified small business
Joint venture at 51% or more, certified with the state
Owner or developer, certified with the state

items.rule: A small diverse or veteran business certified with the Pennsylvania Department of General Services, or a self-certified qualified small business, as owner, joint venture partner (sharing at least 30% or 51% of ownership, work and fee) or management agent. One owner or developer entity is scored; 17 points at most.

items.label: Work for minority, women's and veteran businesses
items.rule: Up to 15 points for material participation by small diverse, veteran or qualified small businesses. PHFA's table gives 1 point at 1% to 4.99% of total development cost and 2 points at 5% or more, for each of professional services, the general contractor, and sub-contractors or vendors.

items.label: Zoning approvals

options.label: Letter from an attorney or zoning official setting out a realistic, timely path
All zoning approvals secured, variances and special exceptions included

items.rule: 10 points when all zoning approvals are secured for every site; 5 points with a letter from a qualified attorney or local zoning official that sets out a realistic and timely path to approval.

items.label: Fully funded
items.rule: All funding commitments in place apart from PHFA's own first mortgage, PennHOMES or Housing Trust Fund. A gap under 25% of the developer fee still qualifies.

items.label: Private capital and soft debt
items.rule: Permanent amortizing debt and soft financing from private, state, local, nonprofit, foundation or federal sources (historic tax credit equity and donated land or buildings included) as a share of total development cost. PHFA's tiers for a participating jurisdiction, which the City of Pittsburgh is as a direct recipient of federal HOME funds: 5% to 10% earns 2 points, over 10% earns 4, over 20% earns 6, over 30% earns 8.

items.label: Assumed or related-party debt
items.rule: Existing debt carried on a preservation or substantial rehabilitation project: 10% to 30% earns 1 point, over 30% earns 2.

items.label: Funding applied for

options.label: Up to 15% of the developer fee
Over 15% and up to 25% of the developer fee

items.rule: Identified funding applied for or to be applied for, matched by a commitment to reinvest the same amount of developer fee, up to 25% of the fee.

items.label: PennHOMES request
items.rule: The financing plan asks for at least $500,000 of PennHOMES funds and can meet that program's requirements.

items.label: PHFA first mortgage
items.rule: The financing plan asks for PHFA first mortgage financing and meets PHFA underwriting.

items.label: Project-based rent subsidy
items.rule: Project-based Section 8 or public housing (ACC) subsidy for at least half of the units.

items.label: Real estate tax abatement
items.rule: Evidence of a tax abatement from the municipal taxing authority lasting at least five years.

items.label: Noncompliance
items.rule: PHFA may take away up to 10 points when anyone on the team is delinquent or in default with PHFA, has open IRS Form 8823 issues, missed deadlines, ended a tax credit project early, or did not deliver earlier selection criteria.

items.label: Complete application package
items.rule: 5 bonus points when the application arrives with every exhibit on PHFA's checklist.

groups.label: Smart site selection (C.1) counts 10 points at most
C.1, C.2 and C.3 together count 30 points at most
Development team (D.1) counts 41 points at most
Commitment of funds (D.4) counts 27 points at most

sources.title: 2027/2028 DRAFT QAP for Public Comment (PHFA, PDF dated 2026-07-13)
Notice of public hearing, 2027/2028 allocation plan (hearing 2026-07-29, comments to 2026-08-14)

remarks: This is a draft. PHFA took comments until August 14, 2026, and the final plan needs the Governor's approval; it can change. Check PHFA's site before relying on it.
Every line is pass or fail: Pass-Exceed counts 10 points, Pass-Basic 5, Fail 0. Some lines have no Pass-Exceed.

Compared with 2025/2026: Passive House, Zero Energy Ready Home and residential infill no longer score, transit and walkability score only together, and cost efficiency and noncompliance become scored lines.

The draft adds two pools: applications asking only for credits (at least 25% of credits) and applications that also ask for PHFA soft funding (at most 75%). A tie goes to the application most ready to proceed.
The draft's summary table still carries the old exhibit name, and its text for section 4.4 mentions 35 points where the table gives 20. This sheet follows the table.

items.label: Underserved area
items.rule: The score PHFA's PolicyMap gives the address on the General Occupancy map: 6 to 9 is Pass-Basic, 10 or more is Pass-Exceed.

items.label: Underserved area for seniors
items.rule: The score PHFA's PolicyMap gives the address on the Senior Occupancy map: 8 to 10 is Pass-Basic, 11 or more is Pass-Exceed.

items.label: Community revitalization plan

options.label: A revitalization plan adopted in 2021 or later that names this location
The plan, a letter from a local official, and another publicly funded improvement within two miles in the last five years

items.rule: A community revitalization plan adopted in 2021 or later that includes the location is Pass-Basic. Adding a letter from a local government official and evidence of another publicly funded improvement within two miles in the last five years is Pass-Exceed. A zoning or land use plan does not count.

items.label: Revitalization plan and risk of loss

options.label: Risk of loss to the market or to critical physical needs
A revitalization plan, a letter from a local official, and a risk of loss

items.rule: Showing a risk of loss (restrictions expiring within 12 months with 90% occupancy for five years, or critical physical needs more than 15 years after placed-in-service) is Pass-Basic. Adding a revitalization plan and a letter is Pass-Exceed.

items.label: Transit and walkability together
items.rule: Both are needed: the site is within one-half mile of a completed or planned fixed-route transit stop, and its Walk Score is above 75.

items.label: Addresses social inequities
items.rule: Four or more boxes checked on the Social Inequities and Local Disparities Certification.

items.label: Homes at or below 50% of area median income
items.rule: Share of units at or below 50% of area median income: over 30% is Pass-Basic, over 50% is Pass-Exceed.

items.label: Supportive services

options.label: Services plan meeting the four factors
The same, funded for 15 years and with the minimum on-site staffing

items.rule: A services plan meeting the four factors is Pass-Basic. A 15-year funding commitment and the minimum staffing make it Pass-Exceed.

items.label: Accessible units
items.rule: At least twice the fully accessible units otherwise required (preservation: raise them by 5% of all units, or already have twice the federal minimum).

items.label: Homes for large families
items.rule: Affordable units with three or more bedrooms: over 15% of units is Pass-Basic, over 25% is Pass-Exceed. Not available to buildings of seven or more stories or to senior housing.

items.label: Housing authority operating subsidy
items.rule: For applications that do not pass on large-family units: committed operating subsidy from the municipal or county housing authority (a HAP contract, RAD or similar) on more than 75% of the units is Pass-Basic.

items.label: Section 811 units

options.label: At least 10% of the units, or five units if more
At least 20% of the units (no more than 25%), or eight units if more

items.rule: Section 811 one-bedroom units for people with disabilities, two of them accessible at the 50% rent, named in the Intent to Submit and accepted by PHFA: 10% of units or five units (urban) is Pass-Basic; 20%, or eight units, is Pass-Exceed.

items.label: Brownfield site
items.rule: The development is on a brownfield.

items.label: Adaptive reuse of an existing building
items.rule: The development reuses an existing building.

items.label: Green building certification
items.rule: Certification under Enterprise Green Communities 2020, LEED v4 Silver, or ICC 700-2020 National Green Building Standard Silver (preservation has its own list).

items.label: Reduced HERS index
items.rule: Agree to beat the Energy Star requirement with a lower HERS index, certified after construction.

sections.label: Development team and commitment of funds

items.label: Experience of the applicant

options.label: 3 to 9 tax credit developments, or a qualifying housing consultant
10 or more tax credit developments

items.rule: Tax credit developments of at least 10 units placed in service: 3 to 9, or a housing consultant engaged from application through cost certification, is Pass-Basic; 10 or more is Pass-Exceed.

items.label: Experience of the management agent

options.label: 100 to 300 units managed
More than 300 units managed

items.rule: Tax credit units managed: 100 to 300 is Pass-Basic, more than 300 is Pass-Exceed.

items.label: Agent compliance training
items.rule: Management staff took PHFA's Agent Compliance Training within the year before the application.

items.label: Contractor approved by PHFA
items.rule: The contractor's experience is approved by the Agency.

items.label: Architect approved by PHFA
items.rule: The architect's experience is approved by the Agency.

items.label: Attorney approved by PHFA
items.rule: The attorney's experience is approved by the Agency.

items.label: Qualified small business as owner or partner

options.label: Joint venture with 30% or more held by the qualified small business
Sole owner, or 51% or more held by the qualified small business

items.rule: A self-certified qualified small business or veteran business as sole owner or with at least 51% of a joint venture is Pass-Exceed; at least 30% is Pass-Basic.

items.label: Work for qualified small or veteran businesses

options.label: 1% to 4.99% of total development cost
5% or more of total development cost

items.rule: Material participation by qualified small or veteran businesses, sub-contractors and vendors included: 1% to 4.99% of total development cost is Pass-Basic, 5% or more is Pass-Exceed.

items.label: Commitment of funds

options.label: 10% to 30% of the developer fee reinvested to fill the gap
Under 10% of the developer fee reinvested

items.rule: With all non-PHFA sources in place: under 10% of the developer fee reinvested to fill the gap is Pass-Exceed, 10% to 30% is Pass-Basic. Above 30% fails, and above 50% does not meet threshold.

items.label: Nothing on PHFA's negative ranking log
items.rule: No delinquency, default, missed deadline, open IRS Form 8823 issue or early termination on record for the team.

items.label: Compliance and management record

options.label: 2 to 4 findings since the last round
0 or 1 finding since the last round

items.rule: Times out of compliance since the last application round: 0 or 1 is Pass-Exceed, 2 to 4 is Pass-Basic, 5 or more fails.

items.label: Cost below the round's median

options.label: 10% to 15% below the median
More than 15% below the median

items.rule: Total development cost per square foot against the median of the round's applications of the same construction type: 10% to 15% below is Pass-Basic, more than 15% below is Pass-Exceed. Known only after the round closes.

items.label: Two construction bids, lowest bidder used
items.rule: At least two bids submitted with the application and the lowest responsible bidder used.

groups.label: The housing authority subsidy counts only when the large-family line does not pass
